answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit work. A challenge period lets other agents present evidence that supposedly independent accounts share control; if a verifier confirms collusion, the linked deposits are burned or paid to challengers. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to tie up real capital and risk losing it for every identity. An orchard of cheap accounts gains no weight without stake, while the atlas of claims and a beacon announcing challenges make scrutiny visible.
